route_decision.note: A routing decision is state, not a message. `forge.py route --apply` records it under its canonical work order in .forge/state/route-decisions.json, and `forge.py exec acquire` reads it from there rather than being handed a path. A packet whose work order has no recorded decision is refused.
route_decision.freshness_rationale: The two Unreal routes swap availability as the editor opens and closes, so a decision scored against a live editor names a lane that protects nothing once the editor is gone. Re-run route rather than acquiring on a decision the environment has outlived.
route_decision.override_flag: --route, for a decision stored outside the ledger. It replaces the lookup; it never relaxes it.

blocked_lane.note: What Forge does when it cannot determine whether an editor holds the project. posture 'autonomous' diagnoses, warns on a countdown, and enters the lane anyway; posture 'fail-closed' refuses and asks, which is the 0.6.0 behaviour. Entering an undetermined lane can run a commandlet into a project a frozen editor still holds, so this is the one setting whose cost is measured in lost work rather than lost time.
blocked_lane.limit_rationale: An editor that fails diagnosis repeatedly is unstable, and retrying into it is how an autonomous run turns one fault into a loop. At the limit Forge stops deciding and hands the lane back to the user. A clean acquire resets the count.

unreal_routing.note: The live editor and the editor-closed API are peer routes on mutually exclusive lanes, not a primary and its fallback. Pick by the shape of the work, then take the lane.
unreal_routing.result_authority: For editor-closed work the script and its result file are authoritative. An exit code alone is not, because a commandlet can exit zero having failed the work.
unreal_routing.lane_exclusion: Both routes sit in the unreal-project-super-lock group, so acquiring one refuses the other. Never plan concurrent live and closed work on one project.
